title: What is known about 1RB0LC_0RC0RF_1RD0LE_1LA1RA_1LC1RB_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_0RC0RF_1RD0LE_1LA1RA_1LC1RB_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open; analysis only begun. Sampled when the head is in E at the left end, the tape is a list of blocks of the words 0100, 0010 and 0001, as in E> (10)^2 (0100)^189 (10)^3 (0010)^633 (01)^2 (0001)^n plus a short tail. All blocks but the last are frozen. The last one grows by a factor of about 1.4 per event: n = 13, 159, 363, …, 28,645, 40,230 up to step 1.9·1010. From time to time a new level begins: 189 copies of 0100 froze at step 0.43·106, and 633 copies of 0010 at step 9.1·106. The exact map and the halting condition are further work.
Third pass. No halt in 1018 steps (macro simulation); the third level froze at 40,231 copies and a fourth grows. The growth factor 1.40 is 7/5 (community tracker: a recursive counter).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The shape of the run from blank tape
claims.text: The E-events at the left end up to 1.93·1010 steps have the form described: a frozen prefix (10)^2 (0100)^189 (10)^3 (0010)^633 (01)^2 since step 9.1·106, then (0001)^n with n = 13, 159, 363, 649, 1050, 1612, 2398, 3499, 5039, 7197, 10215, 14443, 20361, 28645, 40230, then a short tail (0^5 1^2, (001)^2 1, 0^2 1^2, …). At the last event the tail is 0^2 (10)^2 (0010)^7 0^2 1^2, which looks like the start of a new level.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>18</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells, whole runs of equal blocks crossed at once, exact step counts) runs 10<sup>18</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt. The block of 40,230 copies of the first analysis froze at 40,231 and a new level grows behind it.
claims.where: holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA/py/check_msim.py run 1RB0LC_0RC0RF_1RD0LE_1LA1RA_1LC1RB_0RB--- 1e18 (macro simulator c/msim.c there, checked against the direct simulator at 109 steps by check_msim.py check)

claims.title: No pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states
claims.text: The pushdown reduction of bb6-1RB0LF_1RC0LB/c/pds.c (one side of the tape kept exactly, the other abstracted by a DFA, reachability by post* saturation) reaches a halt for every DFA with at most 6 states, on either side: TM=1RB0LC_0RC0RF_1RD0LE_1LA1RA_1LC1RB_0RB--- ./pds 6 L and R.

claims.title: The map and the halting condition
claims.text: The growth ratio of the last block is not constant (1.44 falling to 1.40), and the tail changes from event to event, so the event map has more structure than a single number. During a sweep 14 copies of the middle block move at a time. No halting configuration of a high-level map has been identified yet.

explainer.lede: Not known yet. The tape fills up with long blocks of a repeated four-cell word. Only the last block keeps growing, by about 40% per sweep of the head, and the earlier ones stay frozen. Now and then a new block with a new word is started. How it could halt is still to be found.

facts.text: No halt in the macro simulator (checked against the direct one at 10<sup>9</sup>).
Growth of the last block per sweep, while the earlier blocks stay frozen.
No halt, proved in Lean (first 10,000 by the kernel).

sections.heading: Frozen blocks and one growing block
html: When the head is in state E at the left end, the tape reads, from left to right, (10)^2 (0100)^189 (10)^3 (0010)^633 (01)^2 (0001)^n and a short tail. Only n changes: 13, 159, 363, 649, 1,050, 1,612, 2,398, 3,499, 5,039, 7,197, 10,215, 14,443, 20,361, 28,645, 40,230, a factor of about 1.4 per sweep.

The frozen blocks are what is left of earlier levels. The block of 0100 grew to 189 copies and froze at step 432,110, and the block of 0010 grew to 633 copies and froze at step 9.1 million. At step 1.9·1010 the tail 0^2 (10)^2 (0010)^7 0^2 1^2 may be the start of the next level.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.078). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.536).
After 109 steps the tape spans 35,260 cells (58 left of the start, 25,847 right), with a density of 1s of 0.449.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A growing list of frozen blocks: the last block of the tape grows by a factor of about 1.4 per sweep while the earlier blocks stay fixed, and from time to time a new level with a new word starts; the map and halting condition are not yet known.
family: List of frozen blocks with a last block growing by about 1.4 per sweep
